$description: HIGH-CONTRAST DARK semantic palette — the fifth theme, for users who need maximum contrast *and* dark surfaces. Emitted under [data-theme="high-contrast-dark"]. Previously this combination existed only as a hand-written @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) and (prefers-contrast: more) remap in the generated index.css, which meant it was invisible to JS and native consumers and could not be explicitly selected by a user whose OS preferences did not happen to report both. Surfaces drop to pure black so foreground contrast is maximized rather than merely improved; brand hues rise to their 200–400 steps, which are the light end of each ramp and therefore the high-contrast direction on dark. Chart series swap to the CVD-safe high-contrast variants in the generated index.css.

primary.$description: Pure black — maximum-contrast dark base. Unlike the dark theme's Midnight Court, this trades brand warmth for headroom.

elevated.$description: Elevated surface — cards, popovers, inputs. Paired with a lavender-gray border, since elevation on black must be conveyed by border, not by a shadow no one can see.

raised.$description: JRM extension (deepest chrome) — legacy --color-surface-3 alias. The most demanding surface for foreground contrast, so every status token below is measured against it.

secondary.$description: Muted by role, not by low contrast — still clears AAA on every surface in this theme.

disabled.$description: Disabled text — WCAG-exempt, but kept legible rather than dimmed to the dark theme's court-line.

inverse.$description: Black text on light interactive fills.

default.$description: Near-max element definition on dark. Borders carry the structural load that shadows cannot on a black base.
Royal Violet raised two steps past the dark theme's 400 for AAA-range contrast on black.

ink.$description: Gold text on dark surfaces lightens one step past the dark theme's 500.

positive.$description: Pair with icon+text — never color alone.

pending.$description: In-flight, processing, syncing. Pair with an icon or label; never signal state by hue alone.

positiveSubtle.$description: Low-emphasis fills use the 700 step here, not the 900 the dark theme uses. A 'subtle' fill and a high-contrast theme are inherently in tension: 900 carries white text at 15.71:1 but sits only 1.08:1 against background-elevated, so the fill itself is imperceptible to the very users this theme exists for. 700 is the only step that clears AA for white text (5.24–6.46:1 across the hues) while keeping the fill boundary visible — 3.25–4.01:1 against background-primary, satisfying WCAG 1.4.11. On background-elevated the warmest hues land at 2.62:1, which is why every subtle fill in this theme must also carry border.default; that border is the boundary of record, and this theme already mandates it because shadows are invisible on a black base.

neutralSubtle.$description: The lightest ink step that still carries white text well above AA (12.06:1). No neutral step reaches 3:1 against the elevated surface, so like every subtle fill in this theme it depends on border.default for its boundary.
